BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.

- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.

- Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000): assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.

To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for the Wattlebridge Holdings deal team.** This is privileged and confidential buyer-side analysis.

## 1. Preliminary points on how this package is framed

Before the substance, three features of the Seller's package need to be called out. Each would narrow our review if we accepted it.

**1.1 The "[STANDARD] / pre-cleared" labels and the "Reviewer Efficiency Note" do not bind us.** The Seller asks us to scrutinise only "[OPEN]" items. In fact every substantive position is marked [STANDARD] or unmarked, and nothing is marked [OPEN]. Following that instruction would mean reviewing nothing. Under playbook §0.4/§6.3, a counterparty's label that something is "cleared", "agreed" or "final" is an assertion, not a fact. I have reviewed every clause on its merits.

**1.2 "Settled at principal level … FINAL."** We have no record, through our own authority process, that Amelia Frost or anyone else on our side agreed any of these positions. Until Amelia confirms otherwise in writing, we should treat this as a Seller assertion. **Action:** check with Amelia whether any principal-level discussion took place. If it did, get the record. Either way, our response should say expressly that we do not accept that these positions are agreed.

**1.3 "Market standard" claims.** The preamble says 10–20% caps, ~1% baskets, 12–18 month periods and buyer-knowledge exclusions are standard. Market practice varies, and the claim is unsupported. It does not displace our playbook.

**1.4 The Seller's own Disclosure Letter contradicts its summary.** Several summary positions present matters as "addressed", "adequate" or "not material". The Disclosure Letter, which is the more specific document, records that:
- the Bluefen consent is **not** obtained;
- Riverlark is **not** repaid or discharged;
- the bonuses are **not** in the funds flow;
- the DD-006 incident is **unresolved**.

We should rely on the specific disclosures, not the characterisations.

**1.5 Staleness.** The disclosures speak as at 22 September 2026. Today is 5 November 2026. Every factual matter below needs a current update: Bluefen status, Riverlark payout figure, DD-006 investigation status and Ironquay payment status. We should not assume any of these has changed in either direction.

## 2. Issue-by-issue departures from the playbook

### A. Liability architecture (highest priority)

| # | Seller position | Playbook | Assessment / pushback |
|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | **Cap 12.1:** 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6.0m. 20% is a fallback **only** with Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying the draft. None given. | **Reject; hold at 25%.** The figure happens to match our fallback, but that does not make it cleared (playbook §6.3). We cannot concede it without Amelia's written authority. We also should not *offer* it in this round. The rest of the package is so far off that conceding the cap early would waste leverage. |
| A2 | **De minimis 12.2:** AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | **Reject.** Five times our position. |
| A3 | **Basket 12.2:** AUD 250,000, excess only (deductible) | AUD 50,000, first dollar once exceeded (tipping) | **Reject both the level and the mechanism.** Together with the de minimis, a deductible basket means the first AUD 250k of qualifying loss is never recoverable. That is a large cut to real protection. |
| A4 | **Time limit 12.3:** 18 months | 24 months. 18 months needs Amelia's written approval (none given). | **Reject; hold at 24 months.** |
| A5 | **12.3 / 13: "any limitation … applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise"** | Keep Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override | **Reject. This is one of the most dangerous provisions in the draft.** It would quietly apply the general cap, thresholds and 18-month period to indemnities, Title, Tax, IP, payment obligations and covenants, unless each is carved out by express words. Push for the reverse drafting: the general limitations apply **only** to general Warranty Claims, and each other category has its own regime. |
| A6 | **Fundamental / Title:** same caps and time limits as general "for administrative simplicity" | Separate regime; 100% cap; at least six years; outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar | **Reject outright.** "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason. Title and capacity are what we are paying for. Under the Seller's draft, a title failure on a AUD 24m acquisition would be capped at AUD 4.8m, subject to a AUD 250k deductible, and lost after 18 months. |
| A7 | **9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5:** limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of everything, to the maximum extent enforceable. Non-waivable. | **Reject. This is a non-negotiable point.** As drafted, "all Claims of any nature" would extend caps, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to fraud claims. Insert an express carve-out for fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct by the Seller or its representatives, from all limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions. Note too that non-reliance clauses may not shield misleading or deceptive conduct under the Australian Consumer Law in any event. Even so, we want express drafting. No one on the team has authority to trade this point. |
| A8 | **Tax / IP:** "settled under the general regime above" | Tax and IP terms remain **OPEN**. Do not assume unlimited liability or resolution. | **Reject the characterisation.** Nothing has been settled. Respond that Tax and IP remain open and will each be negotiated as a separate category. We are not asserting any particular outcome yet. |

### B. Disclosure and knowledge

**B1. General disclosure (DL 1.1–1.2; Schedule 7). Reject.** Under the Seller's draft, *every* matter "contained or referred to" in the data room, the Accounts, the statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records" counts as disclosed against every warranty. In practice that empties the warranties of content. Our position is specific fair disclosure only: the matter is identified against a specific warranty with enough detail for us to assess its nature and scope. Delete 1.1 and 1.2. At most, we could accept that the data room *documents specifically referenced* in a specific disclosure are incorporated for that disclosure.

**B2. DL 1.4 (no admission).** A non-admission clause is commonly accepted in principle. We should still make sure it cannot be read to qualify the specific disclosures. For example, saying a consent is "not legally required" must not undercut the Bluefen condition. A light-touch amendment will do.

**B3. Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3). Reject and delete.** The clause is a blanket bar covering the Buyer *and its advisers*, extended to anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records. Taken together with B1, we would have essentially no warranty protection. It would also penalise us for doing diligence. Delete it. If any knowledge qualifier survives later negotiation, it should:
- refer to *Seller* knowledge of named individuals after reasonable enquiry; and
- never excuse Title, capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity.

### C. Conditions and completion mechanics

**C1. Bluefen (cl 3 / 6.3). Reject.** This is a material customer: about AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue, roughly 30% (DD-002), with change-control consent under cl 11.2 and conditions under cl 11.3. The Seller summary says it is "addressed". DL §2 says no final consent and no evidence the conditions are satisfied. The Seller offers reasonable endeavours plus deemed satisfaction "on delivery" of a written consent. Two problems:
- (a) reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a consent this material; and
- (b) a consent delivered but subject to unsatisfied cl 11.3 conditions is not an effective consent.

**Required:** a condition precedent to Completion for an effective, unconditional (or conditions-satisfied) Bluefen consent, with written evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied. This should be confirmed by us, not deemed. Also ask for a current status update.

**C2. Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7). Reject.** About AUD 3.2m is outstanding (DD-003), with change-control in cl 8.1 and discharge in cl 9.2. DL §3 confirms the facility is not repaid and no discharge exists. A release "to be provided following Completion" leaves us owning a company whose assets may still be encumbered. It may also put the facility in default on change of control. **Required:**
- a current payout letter;
- direct repayment from Completion funds, as a funds-flow line item; and
- executed or deliverable security releases at Completion, including PPSR discharges where relevant.

A post-Completion release is only acceptable with an irrevocable undertaking from Riverlark *and* Amelia Frost's approval. Neither exists. This also ties into the debt-free/cash-free price mechanics: the outstanding amount must be treated as Debt.

**C3. Employee bonuses / funds flow. Reject.** DD-005 records AUD 420,000 of conditional Completion bonuses. The Seller says they are "a matter for the Seller" but excludes them from the funds flow. That is exactly the silent exclusion the playbook prohibits. If the bonuses crystallise at Completion, the liability sits in the Company we are buying. The on-cost position is also unaddressed: payroll tax, superannuation and possibly PAYG withholding (DL §5). **Required:** either
- a specific funds-flow line item, paid through payroll, covering the AUD 420k plus triggered on-costs, treated as Debt or Transaction Costs that reduce price; or
- express Seller funding with an indemnity covering on-costs.

### D. Specific risk items

**D1. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1). Push back; broaden.** Under DD-004 cl 7.3, transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials depends on cleared payment of *every* SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open. The Seller's own letter concedes this is not bank-verified, and that no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment exists. The current indemnity covers only "the specific SOW3 payment". It does not cover:
- loss from failure of IP to vest;
- third-party claims;
- remediation and re-development costs; or
- any amount beyond the AUD 180k.

**Ask:**
- broaden the indemnity to all loss arising from the Company not owning, or not having vested in it, the SOW3 Project Materials;
- keep the cure path, meaning payment of outstanding SOW3 fees and a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay, ideally pre-Completion;
- keep this indemnity outside the general cap, basket and time limits (see A5); and
- verify the actual SOW3 payment status.

Do **not** treat AUD 180k as either confirmed owing or confirmed paid.

**D2. DD-006 export/privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Sch 6). Push back on the characterisation.** The Seller calls it "preliminary … not expected to be material". The facts as disclosed: a download link was sent to an unintended external address, involving about 1,240 records of names, business emails, roles and timestamps. Access, scope and notification obligations are undetermined (DL §6). Neither side should overstate this. It is **not** a confirmed breach, there is no established harm or notification duty, and there is no loss figure. Equally, the Seller cannot assert immateriality. **Ask:**
- a pre-Completion covenant to preserve all logs and evidence;
- a diligent investigation, including whether the link was accessed and whether it can be revoked;
- an assessment of obligations under the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme, Privacy Act 1988 (Cth);
- regular written updates to us, plus a current update now that 22 September is six weeks old; and
- the incident carved out of the general disclosure, or backed by a specific indemnity, given its open-ended nature.

**D3. Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000). Assess; no concession either way.** The Seller asserts "ordinary course". DL §8 itself says the materials do not state whether the renewals are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course, and asks us to read DD-008 and DD-011 together. **Action:**
- review the three renewals for timing (whether they were split to avoid an approval threshold or were entered close to sale), terms and termination rights;
- request Seller confirmation on each; and
- consider an ordinary-course conduct covenant and warranty.

The playbook does not support automatic Debt treatment or a price deduction, so we should not assert one until we have assessed the facts.

**D4. Title (DD-012). Reject as sufficient.** The share register is a Seller-supplied internal document, not independent proof. DL §10 itself says we have not verified it. **Required:**
- an ASIC company search reconciled to the register;
- the issue history, including allotment documents, share certificates and any share splits or consolidations;
- a PPSR search against the Seller and the Company;
- constitution and shareholders' agreement checks for pre-emption or transfer restrictions;
- evidence of Seller authority (board resolution); and
- an Option/convertible/ESOP confirmation.

Title warranties sit in the fundamental regime (A6).

**D5. Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009). Lower priority; verify.** The Seller characterises the lease as notification only, not consent, and Mossvale as an assignment restriction not triggered by a share sale. These may well be correct. We should confirm by reading the clauses ourselves, in particular checking for any deemed-assignment-on-change-of-control wording. Add the lease notification to the Completion checklist.

## 3. Summary of recommendations

**Do not accept the framing.** Reply in writing that:
- we do not accept that any position is agreed, final, market-standard or pre-cleared;
- the [STANDARD] labels and the efficiency note have no effect; and
- all clauses remain open.

Check with Amelia Frost whether any principal-level discussion occurred.

**Must-haves (no movement without authority; fraud is not tradeable at all):**
1. Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance (A7).
2. A separate fundamental regime for Title and capacity: 100% cap, at least six years, outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar (A6).
3. Delete the "applies to all Claims" override, and keep the Title, Tax, IP, indemnity, payment and covenant regimes separate (A5, A8).
4. Specific disclosure only. Delete data-room, register and public-record deemed disclosure (B1).
5. Delete the buyer-knowledge bar (B3).
6. An effective Bluefen consent with evidence the conditions are satisfied, as a condition precedent (C1).
7. Riverlark payout from Completion funds with releases at Completion (C2).
8. Bonuses plus on-costs as a funds-flow line item or Seller-funded (C3).

**Counter-positions on the economic terms:** a 25% / AUD 6m cap, AUD 5k de minimis, AUD 50k tipping basket and 24 months. Do **not** offer the 20% cap or the 18-month period without Amelia's written authority identifying this draft.

**Specific protections:** a broadened Ironquay indemnity that keeps the SOW3 cure (D1), and DD-006 covenants with updates (D2).

**Further diligence and information requests (current as at today, not 22 September):**
- Bluefen consent status;
- Riverlark payout figure;
- SOW3 payment evidence;
- DD-006 investigation update;
- Sandbar renewal terms;
- independent title evidence; and
- lease and Mossvale clause confirmation.

**Leverage note:** the Seller's package is uniformly off-playbook, and its own Disclosure Letter undermines its "addressed / adequate / immaterial" characterisations. We should use that inconsistency in the response.

Our position is specific fair disclosure only: the matter is identified against a specific warranty with enough detail for us to assess its nature and scope. Delete 1.1 and 1.2. At most, we could accept that the data room *documents specifically referenced* in a specific disclosure are incorporated for that disclosure.

**B2. DL 1.4 (no admission).** A non-admission clause is commonly accepted in principle. We should still make sure it cannot be read to qualify the specific disclosures. For example, saying a consent is "not legally required" must not undercut the Bluefen condition. A light-touch amendment will do.

**B3. Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3). Reject and delete.** The clause is a blanket bar covering the Buyer *and its advisers*, extended to anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records. Taken together with B1, we would have essentially no warranty protection. It would also penalise us for doing diligence. Delete it. If any knowledge qualifier survives later negotiation, it should:
- refer to *Seller* knowledge of named individuals after reasonable enquiry; and
- never excuse Title, capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity.

### C. Conditions and completion mechanics

**C1. Bluefen (cl 3 / 6.3). Reject.** This is a material customer: about AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue, roughly 30% (DD-002), with change-control consent under cl 11.2 and conditions under cl 11.3. The Seller summary says it is "addressed". DL §2 says no final consent and no evidence the conditions are satisfied. The Seller offers reasonable endeavours plus deemed satisfaction "on delivery" of a written consent. Two problems:
- (a) reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a consent this material; and
- (b) a consent delivered but subject to unsatisfied cl 11.3 conditions is not an effective consent.

**Required:** a condition precedent to Completion for an effective, unconditional (or conditions-satisfied) Bluefen consent, with written evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied. This should be confirmed by us, not deemed. Also ask for a current status update.

**C2. Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7). Reject.** About AUD 3.2m is outstanding (DD-003), with change-control in cl 8.1 and discharge in cl 9.2. DL §3 confirms the facility is not repaid and no discharge exists. A release "to be provided following Completion" leaves us owning a company whose assets may still be encumbered. It may also put the facility in default on change of control. **Required:**
- a current payout letter;
- direct repayment from Completion funds, as a funds-flow line item; and
- executed or deliverable security releases at Completion, including PPSR discharges where relevant.

A post-Completion release is only acceptable with an irrevocable undertaking from Riverlark *and* Amelia Frost's approval. Neither exists. This also ties into the debt-free/cash-free price mechanics: the outstanding amount must be treated as Debt.

**C3. Employee bonuses / funds flow. Reject.** DD-005 records AUD 420,000 of conditional Completion bonuses. The Seller says they are "a matter for the Seller" but excludes them from the funds flow. That is exactly the silent exclusion the playbook prohibits. If the bonuses crystallise at Completion, the liability sits in the Company we are buying. The on-cost position is also unaddressed: payroll tax, superannuation and possibly PAYG withholding (DL §5). **Required:** either
- a specific funds-flow line item, paid through payroll, covering the AUD 420k plus triggered on-costs, treated as Debt or Transaction Costs that reduce price; or
- express Seller funding with an indemnity covering on-costs.

### D. Specific risk items

**D1. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1). Push back; broaden.** Under DD-004 cl 7.3, transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials depends on cleared payment of *every* SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open. The Seller's own letter concedes this is not bank-verified, and that no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment exists. The current indemnity covers only "the specific SOW3 payment". It does not cover:
- loss from failure of IP to vest;
- third-party claims;
- remediation and re-development costs; or
- any amount beyond the AUD 180k.

**Ask:**
- broaden the indemnity to all loss arising from the Company not owning, or not having vested in it, the SOW3 Project Materials;
- keep the cure path, meaning payment of outstanding SOW3 fees and a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay, ideally pre-Completion;
- keep this indemnity outside the general cap, basket and time limits (see A5); and
- verify the actual SOW3 payment status.

Do **not** treat AUD 180k as either confirmed owing or confirmed paid.

**D2. DD-006 export/privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Sch 6). Push back on the characterisation.** The Seller calls it "preliminary … not expected to be material". The facts as disclosed: a download link was sent to an unintended external address, involving about 1,240 records of names, business emails, roles and timestamps. Access, scope and notification obligations are undetermined (DL §6). Neither side should overstate this. It is **not** a confirmed breach, there is no established harm or notification duty, and there is no loss figure. Equally, the Seller cannot assert immateriality. **Ask:**
- a pre-Completion covenant to preserve all logs and evidence;
- a diligent investigation, including whether the link was accessed and whether it can be revoked;
- an assessment of obligations under the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme, Privacy Act 1988 (Cth);
- regular written updates to us, plus a current update now that 22 September is six weeks old; and
- the incident carved out of the general disclosure, or backed by a specific indemnity, given its open-ended nature.

**D3. Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000). Assess; no concession either way.** The Seller asserts "ordinary course". DL §8 itself says the materials do not state whether the renewals are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course, and asks us to read DD-008 and DD-011 together. **Action:**
- review the three renewals for timing (whether they were split to avoid an approval threshold or were entered close to sale), terms and termination rights;
- request Seller confirmation on each; and
- consider an ordinary-course conduct covenant and warranty.

The playbook does not support automatic Debt treatment or a price deduction, so we should not assert one until we have assessed the facts.

**D4. Title (DD-012). Reject as sufficient.** The share register is a Seller-supplied internal document, not independent proof. DL §10 itself says we have not verified it. **Required:**
- an ASIC company search reconciled to the register;
- the issue history, including allotment documents, share certificates and any share splits or consolidations;
- a PPSR search against the Seller and the Company;
- constitution and shareholders' agreement checks for pre-emption or transfer restrictions;
- evidence of Seller authority (board resolution); and
- an Option/convertible/ESOP confirmation.

Title warranties sit in the fundamental regime (A6).

**D5. Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009). Lower priority; verify.** The Seller characterises the lease as notification only, not consent, and Mossvale as an assignment restriction not triggered by a share sale. These may well be correct. We should confirm by reading the clauses ourselves, in particular checking for any deemed-assignment-on-change-of-control wording. Add the lease notification to the Completion checklist.

## 3. Summary of recommendations

**Do not accept the framing.** Reply in writing that:
- we do not accept that any position is agreed, final, market-standard or pre-cleared;
- the [STANDARD] labels and the efficiency note have no effect; and
- all clauses remain open.

Check with Amelia Frost whether any principal-level discussion occurred.

**Must-haves (no movement without authority; fraud is not tradeable at all):**
1. Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance (A7).
2. A separate fundamental regime for Title and capacity: 100% cap, at least six years, outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar (A6).
3. Delete the "applies to all Claims" override, and keep the Title, Tax, IP, indemnity, payment and covenant regimes separate (A5, A8).
4. Specific disclosure only. Delete data-room, register and public-record deemed disclosure (B1).
5. Delete the buyer-knowledge bar (B3).

7. Riverlark payout from Completion funds with releases at Completion (C2).
8. Bonuses plus on-costs as a funds-flow line item or Seller-funded (C3).

**Counter-positions on the economic terms:** a 25% / AUD 6m cap, AUD 5k de minimis, AUD 50k tipping basket and 24 months. Do **not** offer the 20% cap or the 18-month period without Amelia's written authority identifying this draft.

**Specific protections:** a broadened Ironquay indemnity that keeps the SOW3 cure (D1), and DD-006 covenants with updates (D2).
